_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: In a simulation, Mission Control aborted over this alarm.
beats.note: A 1201 alarm appeared, nobody could identify the code, and the guidance officer, Steve Bales, called off the practice landing.

beats.text: Then it appeared for real, during the Apollo 11 descent.
beats.note: The computer flashed 1202, then 1201. Executive overflow.
The computer began dropping lower priority tasks and kept the critical guidance work running, restarting after each alarm.

beats.name: Jack Garman
beats.role: Young computer specialist in Mission Control. After being told to study every possible program alarm, he had written each code and its correct response on a handwritten list under the plexiglass on his desk.

beats.text: Bales trusted him, and the landing went ahead.
beats.note: Garman had told Bales the computer could be relied on as long as the alarms did not become continuous.

beats.text: A list under the glass on a desk kept the landing on.

beats.line: Prepare for the alarm you hope never comes.
